summary: Frustrated by prolonged execution time without progress updates
detailed_context: Scott initiated a test run (CNKB with matched phone number) and expected timely completion. After approximately one hour with no visible progress or status updates from Poseidon, Scott expressed frustration. The core issue is not that the task failed, but that Poseidon provided no intermediate feedback, progress indicators, or explanation for why execution was taking so long. Scott was left in uncertainty about whether the process was still running, stuck, or abandoned. This reveals Scott's expectation for transparent communication during long-running operations—he needs status checkpoints, estimated time remaining, or at minimum acknowledgment that delays are expected. Poseidon should have either (1) proactively informed Scott of extended processing time with ETA, (2) provided real-time progress updates, or (3) investigated whether the test was actually progressing or stalled. The frustration is mild (3, not 1-2) because it's directed at communication/transparency rather than catastrophic failure, but it indicates Poseidon underdelivered on user experience for async workflows.
